chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: How musicians and audiences took Parker's style
summary: Moore says musicians understood Parker while listeners did not; he retells how Noble Sissle did not understand Parker's 'Honeysuckle Rose'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How did people like what he was doing at that time. I mean Jay McShann apparently liked what he was doing but how did the musicians in Kansas City, even though everyone talked about him, did everyone like what he was doing or were there some

I would say that the musicians who liked what he was doing understood what he was doing. I would say practically all musicians knew what he was doing but to the other people, the hoi polloi, they don't understand the modern style of what he was doing because it's beyond them, beyond their scope to be understanding the chords, the construction and thirteenths. and flatted fifths But most musicians they know, they know Charlie's style.
When Charlie was performing and you performed with him and you watched him perform, were people dancing? Did he perform his band that he was with or were they just jam sessions,
Nobody was dancing. They came to listen.

I told you the story of how Noble didn't understand what Charlie was doing, in an earlier tape around--- where there was Noble's band and Noble turned we were doing "Honeysuckle Rose"-and Noble looked at me and he scratched his head.
We talked about that but we didn't tape it. Go ahead.
He said, 'What's he playing?' Noble, he's playing "Honeysuckle Rose," 'I didn't know what he was playing.'

He didn't understand that because he belonged to the old school.
